Meeting: Incident follow-up — checkout timeouts during flash sale
Attendees: Wei (Eng), Alicia (SRE), Tom (Product)

Wei: Post-mortem on Saturday's flash sale. Checkout error rate spiked to 18% during
the first 10 minutes, mostly 504 timeouts. Traffic was about 6x normal peak.

Alicia: Root cause looks like the inventory-check service. It does a synchronous
call per line item to the pricing service, and pricing was the bottleneck —
p99 latency went from 200ms to over 9 seconds under load.

Tom: Customers were seeing spinners and then failures. We lost an estimated
$140K in abandoned carts in that window based on the funnel drop-off.

Wei: The fix isn't complicated in principle — batch the pricing lookups instead of
one call per line item, and add a circuit breaker so checkout degrades gracefully
instead of hanging for 9 seconds per item.

Alicia: Agreed on the circuit breaker. If pricing is unhealthy, we should fail fast
with a clear "try again" message rather than timing out the whole checkout request.

Tom: Can we also just cache pricing more aggressively during known high-traffic
windows? We know flash sales in advance.

Wei: We could, but stale pricing during a sale is risky — if a price changes mid-
sale and we serve cached, that's a real business problem, not just a UX one.
I'd rather fix the batching and add the circuit breaker first, and treat caching
as a separate, carefully-scoped follow-up.

Alicia: What's an acceptable timeout budget for checkout overall? Right now
there's no end-to-end SLA, individual services just have their own timeouts
stacked on top of each other, which is part of why one slow dependency cascades.

Tom: I don't have a number off the top of my head. Let's say checkout should
fail within 5 seconds if something's wrong, rather than 9+ seconds hanging.

Wei: That's a reasonable target but it needs buy-in from whoever owns the overall
checkout SLA — I don't think that's been formally defined anywhere.

Tom: Fair, let's flag that as an open question rather than guess.

Alicia: One more open question — do we need load testing before this ships, given
it's touching the checkout critical path? I don't want to fix one bottleneck and
discover a new one at the next sale.

Wei: Yes, I'd want a load test against Saturday's traffic profile before we call
this done.
